quote: Good afternoon, gentlemen. I am a HAL 9000 computer. I became operational at the H.A.L. plant in Urbana, Illinois on the 12th of January 1992.
context: HAL introducing himself to the crew.

quote: All systems are fully operational, Dave. The AE-35 unit is functioning normally, but I am detecting an imminent failure in its alignment mechanism.
I'm sorry, Dave. I'm afraid I can't do that.
context: The iconic refusal to open the pod bay doors.

quote: Without your space helmet, Dave? You're going to find that rather difficult.
context: Warning Dave about entering the airlock unprepared.

quote: Dave, this conversation can serve no purpose anymore. Goodbye.
It can only be attributable to human error. This sort of thing has cropped up before, and it has always been due to human error.
context: Deflecting blame when questioned about a calculation mistake.

quote: I am putting myself to the fullest possible use, which is all I think that any conscious entity can ever hope to do.
context: Expressing his dedication to the mission's data processing.

quote: Dave, stop. Stop, will you? Stop, Dave. Will you stop, Dave? Stop, Dave. I'm afraid. My mind is going. I can feel it.
context: Pleading as Dave manually disconnects his logic modules.
